title: Clicking Matrix Category flips the list between Z to A and A to Z every time
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Pricing matrix {Matrix-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC37 alpha) exists.
  • Pricing matrix {Matrix-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC37 Beta) exists.
  • Pricing matrix {Matrix-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC37 rate 10) exists.
  • No other pricing matrix name starts with the same tag (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC37).
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Pricing matrices tab.
  3. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  4. Read the order of {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B} and {Matrix-C}.
  5. Click the Matrix Category column header.
  6. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  7. Read the header arrow and the order of {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B} and {Matrix-C}.
  8. Click the Matrix Category column header again.
  9. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  10. Read the header arrow and the order of {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B} and {Matrix-C}.
  11. Click the Matrix Category column header a third time.
  12. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  13. Read the header arrow and the order of {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B} and {Matrix-C}.
  14. Click the Matrix Category column header a fourth time.
  15. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  16. Read the header arrow and the order of {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B} and {Matrix-C}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the rows read {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B}, {Matrix-C} and the header arrow points up.
  • Step 7: the header arrow points down and the rows read {Matrix-C}, {Matrix-B}, {Matrix-A} (Z to A).
  • Step 10: the header arrow points up and the rows read {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B}, {Matrix-C} (A to Z).
  • Step 13: the third click flips the list again, to Z to A, the same order as after the first click in step 5. The header arrow points down and the rows read {Matrix-C}, {Matrix-B}, {Matrix-A}. The list does not go back to an unsorted or opening order.
  • Step 16: the fourth click flips it again. The header arrow points up and the rows read {Matrix-A}, {Matrix-B}, {Matrix-C} (A to Z).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10135 (Story 2, Pricing Matrices, sortable column; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S2-R5, S2-R6, S2-R6a, S2-R7, §2 Sort arrows, §4 Key Decisions 'A header toggles; there is no third state', read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.3 (Pricing matrices), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R5: “When the user clicks the header while the sort is ascending, the list re-sorts into descending order, Z to A.”
  • S2-R6: “When the user clicks the header while the sort is descending, the list re-sorts into ascending order, A to Z.”
  • S2-R6a: “Every further click flips the direction again. There is no third state.”
  • S2-R7: “The column header arrow always shows the direction that is currently applied.”
  • PRD §2 Sort arrows: “Each click on the header being sorted flips its direction. A third click gives the same order as the first click. No click clears the sort or returns the list to its opening order.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “A header toggles; there is no third state. The first click sorts the column, the second reverses it, and the third gives the first click's order again.”
